posts:
Canada claims to support the International Criminal Court, but stays silent when its own judge is sanctioned by the US.

Ottawa tight-lipped on joining...
Evidence: Rule of law, Silent diplomacy, US relations
#Aletheia #ICC #Canada

Canada claims to be a strong supporter of the ICC and the independence of its judges as a core foreign policy value.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

In reality, Ottawa refuses to support Canadian judge Kimberly Prost against US sanctions to avoid diplomatic friction with Washington.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Deception.
Canada prioritizes bilateral relations over its stated commitment to international law.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (R_net: 1.8, Uncertainty z: 1)
Canadian ICC judge Kimberly Prost is suing the US administration over sanctions that restrict her daily life, but Ottawa refuses to intervene or file an amicus brief.

The Bright Side:
While silent publicly, Canada remains a founding member and financial supporter of the ICC, keeping the institution functional.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a lyrical error (WHY). The narrative of defending human rights is honest only until it conflicts with US relations.

It is a structural bait-and-switch.

Social Physics Analysis:
Ottawa prioritizes political self-preservation over systemic empowerment. By remaining silent, they avoid conflict with a powerful ally, projecting support while acting with neglect.

The Trajectory: Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Diplomatic caution overrides moral duty.

The Unavoidable Truth: Canada is avoiding a dispute with the US.

The Unavoidable Lie: Canada always stands up for the independence of ICC judges.

Alethekanon:
This silence reveals a clear double standard. True commitment to international law requires defending its operators, even when politically inconvenient.

Awwthekanon:
It must feel so lonely for Judge Prost to stand up for justice worldwide while her own home country stays quiet. She deserves real support.

Brothekanon:
Classic diplomatic fence-sitting. You love the ICC until Uncle Sam gets mad, then suddenly you have 'no comment.' Pick a side!
